p: A day at Gulliver's Kingdom is best planned as a full day. The hillside layout means a fair bit of walking, so bring a pushchair suitable for slopes if you have toddlers, and pack snacks and drinks. Arriving early gives you a head start on the most popular rides, and a picnic on the hill can save you money and time. Older children may find it a little tame, so it's best suited to younger kids.

Down in the village, the Peak District Lead Mining Museum tells the story of the miners who worked these hills, with a chance to explore a recreated mine. The valley is part of the Derwent Valley Mills World Heritage Site, and just down the road Cromford Mills, where Richard Arkwright built his pioneering cotton mill, is a fascinating step back in time with a visitor centre and canal-side walks.

If you're visiting in the autumn, look out for the Matlock Bath Illuminations, when illuminated boats glide along the river after dark and the village sparkles. Matlock Bath has a station on the Derwent Valley line from Derby, so it's easy to get here by train. Motorcyclists often gather along the parade on sunny weekends, adding a bit of buzz to the village. Before you head home, grab some fish and chips from one of the riverside chippies and enjoy them on the bank of the Derwent.
